request.spec:
A paste box takes lines of name,amount,date,note (the note may hold commas; the date may be
blank for the sheet's today; the note may be absent) and adds a DRAFT claim per line, in order,
for the named person (the name must be on the sheet, matched as names are compared). Every line is
checked first with exactly the claim form's rules: if any line fails, an error shows on the box
and nothing is added; otherwise every claim is added and written as CLAIM_ADDED. Show how many
were added.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A paste box takes lines of name,amount,date,note (the note may hold commas; the date may be
blank for the sheet's today; the note may be absent) and adds a DRAFT claim per line, in order,
for the named person (the name must be on the sheet, matched as names are compared). Every line is
checked first with exactly the claim form's rules: if any line fails, an error shows on the box
and nothing is added; otherwise every claim is added and written as CLAIM_ADDED. Show how many
were added.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The paste box works: `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{id}/claims/paste`, in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/paste/`. It reads every line first. Each line is split on its first three commas, so the note can hold commas. The date may be blank (the sheet's today) and the note may be left off. The name must match someone on the sheet, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, which is how names are already compared. The amount must have at most two decimals.
- **Claim rules:** each line then goes through the existing claim-add code, so it gets exactly the claim form's checks: no date inside a closed period, nothing after the person retired, and no negative amount (the paste can't say which claim a negative amount corrects). All lines are added in one transaction. If any line fails, the whole paste is undone. Nothing is stored, and no `CLAIM_ADDED` line is written to the audit file, because audit lines are only written once the change is saved.
- **Front end:** a new paste box, `features/claims/paste-claims.ts`, sits under the quick-add bar. It clears the old count and error when you press the button, shows an error when the paste is refused, and otherwise shows how many claims were added. The new claims are listed newest first, so the last line's claim comes out on top.

**Choices beyond the request:**
- Blank lines are skipped, and a paste with no lines at all is refused.
- On a refused paste, the error only says that a line was refused. The server builds a message naming the line and the reason, but the app's server settings don't send error messages to the browser, so it isn't shown.
- After a successful paste, the text stays in the box.
